ar_fern_north.blurb: Fern North is a small sandstone section of the Fern climbing area in the Boston Mountains of northwest Arkansas, a short stroll upstream of the PK Boulder approach. Sixteen routes split between bolted sport lines and traditional climbs, with most ground between 5.7 and 5.10 and a handful at 5.11. Walls here are short, as is typical for Fern, where most lines stay under about 50 feet. A creek runs through the canyon, which makes for a pleasant setting for an easy afternoon of moderates, and a few boulder problems sit nearby for variety. It suits climbers who want quick, approachable lines rather than long days on tall rock.

ar_south_side_albino_rhino_wall.blurb: This sandstone wall belongs to The Throne, a hill in the valley at Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas. Despite the name it sits on the east side of the hill. Reach it by dropping in from the Chickenhead Wall and taking the left fork once you arrive at the Throne; the base is roughly a hundred yards along. Most of the sixteen routes are trad, with a smaller group of bolted sport lines. Grades run from 5.6 up to the low 5.13s, though the bulk fall between 5.9 and 5.11. Expect a mix of crack and face climbing, and a few lines that can also be top-roped.

ar_south_side_2.blurb: South Side is a bouldering zone in the Hurricane Creek area of the Big Piney region, north-central Arkansas. The sandstone blocks sit on the west bank of a small stream that drains toward Hurricane Creek, and you reach them by turning left off the main trail and following flagging across a little rocky creek. Sixteen problems are listed, falling into two camps: a few gentle ones around V0 to V1 and a larger group between V4 and V6. Hurricane Creek as a whole is a quiet, spread-out place, so expect solitude and a steep walk back to the car at the end of the day.

ar_1_schoolhouse.blurb: Schoolhouse is the northernmost of the walls at Fitzgerald South on Fitzgerald Mountain in northwest Arkansas, and the first one you meet on the climbers' trail, about five minutes from the trailhead. Nearly all of its sixteen routes are bolted sport lines, with a single trad option. Mostly vertical sandstone offers friendly climbing between about 5.8 and 5.10, with a few harder pitches into 5.11 and one very easy line. Rock quality ranges from fair to excellent, and some holds are still settling in, so a helmet is worthwhile. Steeper climbing lies in the neighbouring sector to the south.

ar_mullet_buttress.blurb: Mullet Buttress is a compact crag on the east side of the canyon at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, right of the Goat Cave. Most of its sixteen lines are bolted sport routes, joined by a few trad lines and two boulder problems at V3 and V4. Grades cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, with a couple of easier options, so it fits climbers who have moved past the beginner walls. Visitors are few even though several of the lines are good. Spiny brush can crowd the bases in summer, though it is easy to sidestep. Hanging tires above one route help you spot the buttress.

ar_cliffs_of_insanity.blurb: Cliffs of Insanity sits on the east side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, just along from the Roman Wall, which is known as a good spot for newer climbers. From the Roman Wall, continue south to find the cliff. Twelve of its sixteen routes are sport and four are trad. Grades are gentle: nine climbs sit at 5.8, a handful go from 5.5 to 5.7, and only one reaches 5.9. That makes it a solid choice for moderate mileage. The east side faces west, so expect strong sun that can make summer days hot.

ar_tombstone_the.blurb: The Tombstone is one of the crags around Cowell, a tiny backwoods community in north-central Arkansas where there are no services for miles. Sixteen routes are listed, about two thirds bolted and the rest traditional. Difficulty leans toward the middle and upper range: seven lines sit at 5.10, a few reach 5.11, and the remainder are 5.7 to 5.9. Cowell mixes boulder fields, steep sport and adventurous trad, but this crag has no boulder problems or top-rope lines, so bring a rack for the trad lines and plan on a self-sufficient day.

ar_reservation_wall.blurb: Reservation Wall is the standout face at Fern, the small creek-side climbing area in the Boston Mountains of northwest Arkansas. Reach it by the main trail along the bluff and through a narrow corridor; you step out facing the wall. Fourteen of its sixteen routes are bolted sport lines and two are trad. Lines are long for Fern, where most climbs are short, and the rock quality is high. Grades start around 5.6 and are centered on 5.10, with a few at 5.11 and two at 5.12, so it is better for climbers with some lead experience.
